21.text: ADJUDICATED OUTCOME EVENT DEFINITIONS
All cardiovascular endpoint definitions were modifications based on draft recommendations for
CDISC August 20, 2014 (Standardized Definitions for Cardiovascular and Stroke Endpoint Events in
Clinical Trials for CDISC, Hicks KA et al August 2014) and included in the Clinical Endpoint
Committee(CEC) Charter. The CEC Charter specified that in the case of limited or missing data, the
committee was to adjudicate events based on their clinical expertise and the totality of the evidence.
Hospitalization for heart failure
A Heart failure hospitalization should include the following criteria:
1) The adjudicated primary diagnosis is admission to hospital for heart failure.
2) The patient's length-of-stay in hospital extends for at least 12 hours (or a change in calendar
date if the hospital admission and discharge times are unavailable). Emergency room visit for
≥ 12 hours with intravenous therapy would be considered equivalent as admission to
hospital.
3) The patient exhibits documented new or worsening symptoms due to HF on presentation,
including at least ONE of the following:
a. Dyspnea (dyspnea with exertion, dyspnea at rest, orthopnea, paroxysmal dyspnea)
b. Decreased exercise tolerance
c. Fatigue
d. Other symptoms of worsened end-organ perfusion such as dizziness, mental
confusion or volume overload such as weight gain or lower extremity swelling.
4) The patient has objective evidence of new or worsening heart failure, consisting of at least
TWO physical examination findings OR one physical examination finding and at least ONE
laboratory criterion), including:
a. Physical examination findings considered to be due to heart failure, including new or
worsened:
i. Peripheral edema
ii. Increasing abdominal distention or ascites (in the absence of primary hepatic
disease)
iii. Pulmonary rales/crackles/crepitations
iv. Increased jugular venous pressure and/or hepatojugular reflux
v. S3 gallop
vi. Clinically significant or rapid weight gain thought to be related to fluid
retention
b. Laboratory evidence of new or worsening HF, if obtained within 24 hours of
presentation, including:
c. Increased B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP)/ N-terminal pro-BNP (NT proBNP)
concentrations consistent with decompensation of heart failure. In patients with
chronically elevated natriuretic peptides, a significant increase should be noted
above baseline.
d. Radiological evidence of pulmonary congestion
e. Non-invasive diagnostic evidence of clinically significant elevated left- or right-sided
ventricular filling pressure or low cardiac output. For example, echocardiographic
criteria could include: E/e' > 15 or D-dominant pulmonary venous inflow pattern,
plethoric inferior vena cava with minimal collapse on inspiration, or decreased left
ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) minute stroke distance (time velocity integral (TVI)
OR

22.text: f.
Invasive diagnostic evidence with right heart catheterization showing a pulmonary
capillary wedge pressure (pulmonary artery occlusion pressure) ≥ 18 mmHg, central
venous pressure ≥ 12 mmHg, or a cardiac index < 2.2 L/min/m2
5) The patient receives initiation or intensification of treatment specifically for heart failure,
including at least ONE of the following:
a. Augmentation in oral diuretic therapy. NOTE: If the intensification is solely oral diuretics,
the duration of hospitalization must be at least 24 hours.
b. Intravenous diuretic or vasoactive agent (e.g., inotrope, vasopressor, or vasodilator)
c. Mechanical or surgical intervention, including:
i. Mechanical circulatory support (e.g., intra-aortic balloon pump, ventricular assist
device, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, total artificial heart)
ii. Mechanical fluid removal (e.g., ultrafiltration, hemofiltration, dialysis).
An endpoint heart failure hospitalization requires admission to the hospital for heart failure,
worsening of symptoms of heart failure, a duration of hospitalization of at least 12 hours, the
intensification of heart failure therapy, and a committee consensus that the hospitalization was
primarily due to worsening heart failure. Changes in physical signs or laboratory tests,
whenever available and documented, will be considered to be supportive.
Cause of death
Cause of death was adjudicated, as either Cardiovascular death or Non-Cardiovascular death.
Cause of death was further catergorized when possible.
Cardiovascular death includes the following categories:
1. Death due to Acute Myocardial Infarction: refers to a death by any cardiovascular mechanism
(e.g., arrhythmia, sudden death, heart failure, stroke, pulmonary embolus,
peripheral arterial disease) ≤ 30 days after a MI related to the immediate consequences of the MI,
such as progressive heart failure or recalcitrant arrhythmia. We note that there may be assessable
mechanisms of cardiovascular death during this time period, but for simplicity, if the cardiovascular
death occurs ≤ 30 days of the myocardial infarction, it will be considered a death due to myocardial
infarction. Acute MI should be verified to the extent possible by the diagnostic criteria outlined for
acute MI or by autopsy findings showing recent MI or recent coronary thrombosis.
Death resulting from a procedure to treat a MI (percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI),
coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG)), or to treat a complication resulting from MI, should
also be considered death due to acute MI.
Death resulting from an elective coronary procedure to treat myocardial ischemia (i.e.
chronic stable angina) or death due to a MI that occurs as a direct consequence of a CV
investigation/procedure/operation should be considered as a death due to a CV procedure.
2. Sudden cardiac death refers to a death that occurs unexpectedly, not following an acute
MI, and includes the following deaths:
a. Death witnessed and occurring without new or worsening symptoms
b. Death witnessed within 60 minutes of the onset of new or worsening cardiac symptoms,
unless the symptoms suggest acute MI
c. Death witnessed and attributed to an identified arrhythmia (e.g., captured on an
electrocardiographic (ECG) recording, witnessed on a monitor, or unwitnessed but
found on implantable cardioverter-defibrillator review)

23|BACKGROUND
24|Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce the risk of hospitaliza-
25|tion for heart failure in patients regardless of the presence or absence of diabetes.
26|More evidence is needed regarding the effects of these drugs in patients across the
27|broad spectrum of heart failure, including those with a markedly reduced ejection
28|fraction.
29|METHODS
30|In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 3730 patients with class II, III, or
31|IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to receive empagliflozin
32|(10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to recommended therapy. The primary
33|outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for worsening
34|heart failure.
35|RESULTS
36|During a median of 16 months, a primary outcome event occurred in 361 of 1863
37|patients (19.4%) in the empagliflozin group and in 462 of 1867 patients (24.7%)
38|in the placebo group (hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for
39|heart failure, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001). The effect
40|of empagliflozin on the primary outcome was consistent in patients regardless of
41|the presence or absence of diabetes. The total number of hospitalizations for heart
42|failure was lower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (hazard
43|ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001). The annual rate of decline in the esti-
44|mated glomerular filtration rate was slower in the empagliflozin group than in
45|the placebo group (-0.55 vs. -2.28 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area
46|per year, P<0.001), and empagliflozin-treated patients had a lower risk of serious
47|renal outcomes. Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently
48|with empagliflozin.
49|CONCLUSIONS
50|Among patients receiving recommended therapy for heart failure, those in the em-
51|pagliflozin group had a lower risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for
52|heart failure than those in the placebo group, regardless of the presence or absence
53|of diabetes. (Funded by Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly; EMPEROR-Reduced
54|ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03057977.)

49|Methods
50|Trial Design and Oversight
51|Details regarding the design of this randomized,
52|double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled,
53|event-driven trial have been reported previously.5
54|The trial was performed at 520 centers in 20 coun-
55|tries. The protocol and the statistical analysis
56|plan are available (as a single PDF file) with the
57|full text of this article at NEJM.org. The ethics
58|committee at each trial center approved the trial,
59|and all the patients provided written informed
60|consent. The sponsors were Boehringer Ingelheim
61|and Eli Lilly.

68|executive committee provided an independent in-

75|academic trial leadership, and an independent

16|After a screening period of 4 to 28 days, patients
17|who fulfilled the eligibility criteria were randomly
18|assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either empa-

20|addition to their usual therapy for heart failure.
21|The dose of empagliflozin was selected on the
22|basis of the reduction in the risk of cardiovascu-
23|lar death or hospitalization for heart failure that
24|had been previously reported with this dose in
25|patients with type 2 diabetes.7 Randomization
26|was performed with an interactive-response sys-
27|tem that used a permuted-block design and was
28|stratified according to geographical region (North
29|America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, or other),
30|diabetes status at screening, and the estimated
31|glomerular filtration rate (GFR) at screening
32|(<60 or ≥60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-
33|surface area), according to the Chronic Kidney
34|Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI)
35|equation. After randomization, all appropriate
36|treatments for heart failure or other medical con-
37|ditions could be initiated or altered at the clini-
38|cal discretion of the health care provider, accord-
39|ing to each patient's needs.
40|Every 2 to 3 months, we evaluated patients at
41|trial visits to assess outcomes and adverse events.
42|We periodically evaluated vital signs, body weight,
43|glycated hemoglobin level, NT-proBNP level, and
44|renal function. In addition, we assessed the pa-
45|tients' quality of life using the Kansas City Car-
46|diomyopathy Questionnaire. We reevaluated the
47|estimated GFR 23 to 45 days after the discon-
48|tinuation of empagliflozin or placebo in order to

61|ite of adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospi-

63|to the first event. The first secondary outcome
64|was the occurrence of all adjudicated hospital-
65|izations for heart failure, including first and re-
66|current events. The second secondary outcome

8|Discussion
9|In our trial, the combined risk of cardiovascular
10|death or hospitalization for heart failure was 25%
11|lower among the patients who received empa-
12|gliflozin than among those who received place-
13|bo, a difference that was primarily related to a
14|31% lower risk of hospitalization for heart fail-
15|ure. These benefits were seen in patients receiv-
16|ing any of the currently recommended drugs for
17|heart failure, including sacubitril-valsartan, and
18|were seen regardless of the presence or absence
19|of diabetes. In addition, empagliflozin was as-
20|sociated with a lower number of hospitaliza-
21|tions for heart failure and with a slower rate of
22|decline in the estimated GFR; the latter effect
23|was accompanied by a lower risk of serious renal
24|outcomes.
25|Our findings with empagliflozin can be com-
26|pared with the effects of dapagliflozin in the
27|DAPA-HF trial.5 The current trial was enriched
28|for patients with a markedly reduced ejection frac-
29|tion and increased levels of natriuretic peptides,
30|as compared with the patients in the DAPA-HF
31|trial (Table S4). Consequently, the incidence of the
32|primary outcome was approximately 40% higher
33|in the current trial than in the DAPA-HF trial.
34|Our trial thus extends the benefits of SGLT2
35|inhibitors to patients with more advanced but
36|stable heart failure.
37|In both the current trial and the DAPA-HF
38|trial, the benefit of the SGLT2 inhibitor on the
39|primary composite outcome was driven mainly
40|by a reduction in hospitalizations for heart fail-
41|ure. The risk of cardiovascular death was 8%
42|lower with empagliflozin than with placebo in
43|our trial (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.75 to 1.12)
44|and was 18% lower with dapagliflozin in the
45|DAPA-HF trial (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69
46|to 0.98). Of note, in large-scale trials involving
47|patients with type 2 diabetes, the risk reductions
48|in cardiovascular death among patients with
49|similar cardiovascular histories (i.e., those with
50|a prior myocardial infarction) were 41% for em-
51|pagliflozin (hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.44 to
52|0.79) and 8% for dapagliflozin (hazard ratio,
53|0.92; 95% CI, 0.69 to 1.23).7,8 Therefore, as noted
54|by other investigators,1 the effect of SGLT2 in-
55|hibitors on mortality appears to be heteroge-
56|neous, with no consistent evidence that one mem-
57|ber of the drug class is superior to another with
58|respect to the effects on survival.
59|In addition to the observed cardiovascular
60|benefits, empagliflozin slowed the rate of de-
61|cline in the estimated GFR during double-blind
62|treatment, and the risk of the composite renal
63|outcome was lower in the empagliflozin group
64|than in the placebo group. When measurements
65|were compared at the start and the end of the
66|trial after the discontinuation of both empa-
67|gliflozin and placebo, the estimated GFR declined
68|more in the placebo group than in the empa-
69|gliflozin group. These observations are consis-
70|tent with the benefit observed in trials of SGLT2
71|inhibitors in patients with type 2 diabetes who
72|largely did not have heart failure.1 Accordingly,
73|the ability of empagliflozin to favorably influ-
74|ence renal function is apparent in patients with
75|diabetes, in those with heart failure, and in
76|those with both conditions.
77|Uncomplicated genital tract infection was
78|reported more frequently in the empagliflozin
79|group. The frequency of hypoglycemia, lower
80|limb amputation, and bone fracture did not dif-
81|fer between the two groups, even though these
82|adverse events have been associated with the use
83|of certain SGLT2 inhibitors in trials involving
84|patients with type 2 diabetes.9,10 Safety concerns

11|Hospitalization for heart failure
12|
13|A Heart failure hospitalization should include the following criteria:
14|1) The adjudicated primary diagnosis is admission to hospital for heart failure.
15|2) The patient's length-of-stay in hospital extends for at least 12 hours (or a change in calendar
16|date if the hospital admission and discharge times are unavailable). Emergency room visit for
17|≥ 12 hours with intravenous therapy would be considered equivalent as admission to
18|hospital.
19|3) The patient exhibits documented new or worsening symptoms due to HF on presentation,
20|including at least ONE of the following:
21|a. Dyspnea (dyspnea with exertion, dyspnea at rest, orthopnea, paroxysmal dyspnea)
22|b. Decreased exercise tolerance
23|c. Fatigue
24|d. Other symptoms of worsened end-organ perfusion such as dizziness, mental
25|confusion or volume overload such as weight gain or lower extremity swelling.
26|4) The patient has objective evidence of new or worsening heart failure, consisting of at least
27|TWO physical examination findings OR one physical examination finding and at least ONE
28|laboratory criterion), including:
29|a. Physical examination findings considered to be due to heart failure, including new or
30|worsened:
31|i. Peripheral edema
32|ii. Increasing abdominal distention or ascites (in the absence of primary hepatic
33|disease)
34|iii. Pulmonary rales/crackles/crepitations
35|iv. Increased jugular venous pressure and/or hepatojugular reflux
36|v. S3 gallop
37|vi. Clinically significant or rapid weight gain thought to be related to fluid
38|retention
39|b. Laboratory evidence of new or worsening HF, if obtained within 24 hours of
40|presentation, including:
41|c. Increased B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP)/ N-terminal pro-BNP (NT proBNP)
42|concentrations consistent with decompensation of heart failure. In patients with
43|chronically elevated natriuretic peptides, a significant increase should be noted
44|above baseline.
45|d. Radiological evidence of pulmonary congestion
46|e. Non-invasive diagnostic evidence of clinically significant elevated left- or right-sided
47|ventricular filling pressure or low cardiac output. For example, echocardiographic
48|criteria could include: E/e' > 15 or D-dominant pulmonary venous inflow pattern,
